A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of GenKnowSub. Their text, equations, Figure 1, Tables 1–4, references, and Appendices A–B support reliable comparison; relocated appendix content remains available.

before.justification: v1 reports original GenKnowSub evaluations on English reasoning, open-ended generation, and German/French benchmarks using Phi-3 and Phi-2, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in Section 3.3, Tables 1–4, and Appendix B.

M1.justification: Sections 2.1–2.2 retain the same general-knowledge LoRA subtraction and per-token Arrow routing procedure. Equations (1)–(2), language-module variants, and Figure 1 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain clustered Flan and general-language corpus training, nine English reasoning benchmarks, SNI generation tasks, and German/French evaluations. Appendix B retains the same Phi-2 benchmark coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 and the SNI comparison retain Phi-3, Arrow, Shared, and Mean Norm as comparators. Tables 3–4 retain Phi-2 and Arrow; no evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: The reported settings remain unchanged: 20% of each task cluster for Phi-3, full task-cluster data and unquantized weights for Phi-2, and 10,000 SNI examples covering 119 tasks. Zero-shot evaluation, accuracy, and Rouge-L are retained.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the Shared and Mean Norm ablations, comparisons of individual-language versus averaged general modules, and the Phi-2 investigation of dependence on base-model capability. No analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. No statistical reporting procedure changes.

E6.justification: All results in Tables 1–4 and the SNI passage match. For example, Table 1 retains averages of 67.17 for averaged GenKnowSub and 65.56 for Arrow; their SNI Rouge-L scores remain 46.91 and 45.44. Appendix table relocation adds no results.

T1.justification: The residual-module definition, routing-weighted composition, forward-pass expression, and stated assumptions are unchanged. Neither version adds mathematical results, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: general-knowledge subtraction for modular zero-shot transfer and empirical benefits across tasks and languages. Removing the abstract's parenthetical acronym does not alter these claims.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the redundancy-removal interpretation and the qualification that cross-lingual benefits depend on the base model's multilingual capability. Limitations concerning hardware, model diversity, and high-resource language coverage are unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices A–B retain the same quantization, LoRA rank, routing configuration, data preparation, training hyperparameters, hardware, and Phi-2 weight-conversion details. Code, model, and library access information is preserved despite footnote relocation.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged, including the relationships to Arrow, task arithmetic, and jointly trained modular-routing approaches. No reference is added or removed.

P1.justification: v2 updates the University of Tehran affiliation to specify the School of Electrical and Computer Engineering and College of Engineering, and removes '(LLMs)' from the abstract opening. The remaining prose, terminology, and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: v2 reformats the author/contact block, removes printed page numbers, and moves Tables 3–4 from PDF page 10 to page 9, reflowing appendix prose onto page 10. Figure 1 and the tables' contents and structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 makes limited affiliation, wording, and layout edits while preserving the method, experimental evidence, interpretations, limitations, and reproducibility information. The appendix reflow and front-matter changes produce no material overall gain or loss in paper quality.
